Hi Jonas,

- Tracing: your pricing says $0.10 per 10M spans; can you confirm how spans are counted for sampled traces and for trace replays?
- If we exceed the committed retention by 40% in a month, what are the immediate billing mechanics and notification thresholds?

Appreciate any worked examples.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear questions and the usage file. High level answers here plus I'll attach a worked example as a term-sheet page. If you want a one-pager table we can also include it in the contract.

Short answers first:
- Proration: yes, retention and add-on capacity are prorated on a daily basis in the first and last billing cycle. If you start Aug 15 with a 1TB committed retention, you pay pro-rated for the 16 days of Aug (1TB * 16/31) at the committed rate and overage rules begin after the prorated quantity is consumed.
- Tracing spans: we count spans at ingestion time. Sampled traces that are ingested count at the sampled rate. Replayed traces (ingested via replay API) are counted separately and flagged as replay traffic; they are billed at 25% of the ingestion span rate to avoid double-charging for debug replays.
- Overages & notifications: threshold alerts at 80% and 100% of committed retention. Billing is automatic at the overage rate for the month; we also support a soft-block option (opt-in) which pauses ingestion when you hit a hard cap.

Concrete example (we'll put the same in the attached term sheet):
- Commit: 1TB/month at $X/TB (committed rate)
- Aug start Aug 15 -> billed 16/31 of the committed fee for Aug 
- If Aug usage = 1.4TB: you consume your prorated 0.516TB (1TB * 16/31) then pay overage on the extra 0.884TB at the overage per-GB rate

I'll ask Ben to confirm the tracing replay discount and provide the exact overage per-GB number. Marissa, can you confirm what level of crediting (if any) we can offer for a 12-month commit at Horizon's projected volumes?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the table.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Olivia Chen <olivia@horizonanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Telemetry econ models — tracing & retention prorate scenarios

Hey all — digging in on the tracing accounting: a few technical clarifications so Horizon can model costs accurately.

- Span counting: every span object we ingest increments the span counter. If you sample 1:10, only the sampled spans count. If you ingest full traces for replay via our replay ingestion endpoint, those spans are tagged as "replay" and billed at 25% the normal span unit rate.
- Aggregation window: spans are charged in the month they are ingested; late-arriving spans that are backfilled are billed in the month they arrive (not the original event time).
- Trace replay dedupe: if a replay produces duplicate span IDs that match existing ones, we dedupe at the service level and do not bill duplicates. However, replays that are intentionally mutated for debugging will bill.

Overage math example (numbers are illustrative — final per-unit numbers are in the term-sheet PDF):
- Committed: 1TB retention, committed price $200/TB/month
- Overage: $350/TB for incremental usage in the month (billed per GB)
- Aug partial month: prorated committed quantity = 1TB * 16/31 = 0.516TB
- Usage = 1.4TB -> overage billed = (1.4 - 0.516) TB * $350/TB = 0.884 * $350 = $309.4

I'll attach a calculator sheet if helpful.

-ben
Ben Carter
Product Ops — Observability Pricing
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-observability-term-sheet-v2.pdf (pdf, 92KB)

Procurement note: they want payment terms net-45 and a single line item for observability with a breakdown in the SOW.

Best,
Olivia

Jonas — we can offer an introductory protection and a credit structure with these parameters: 

- First-90 cushion: we can cap overage invoicing to max +15% above the committed observability line item for the first 90 days. This is a one-time clause; overages beyond 90 days follow standard billing.
- Discounting: for a 12-month commitment at 1TB/month and an ARR band matching Horizon's forecast, we can provide a 12% committed discount off the published committed price if signed within 30 days. 
- If Horizon prefers an up-front credit instead, we can do a $15k upfront credit applied across months 1-3 in lieu of the percentage discount; choose one option in the SOW.

Procurement terms: Net-45 is acceptable for this account level but we need to confirm legal's review on the single-line SOW format. I'll ask Legal to expedite.

I'll draft the term-sheet edits and include a short billing examples appendix. Jonas, do you want me to include the protection clause language verbatim?

-Marissa

- We prefer the 12% committed discount rather than the upfront credit. Please show the net line item in the SOW reflecting the discount and include the per-GB overage price in parentheses.
- Procurement asks that the invoice cadence be monthly and that the first invoice be prorated for Aug 16–31 as discussed. Net-45 is acceptable.

If you can get an updated term-sheet PDF with those edits today we will circulate internally and aim to sign within the week.
